intentAndPurpose.intent: Horizontal progress bar for determinate (value-driven) or indeterminate loading. Three sizes (S/M/L), pill or flat caps, and multi-accent appearance roles.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent appearance role. Default: `auto` (inherits Surface, else `secondary` at page root).

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: ID of element that labels this progress indicator.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional class name on the root progress element.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Optional test hook — forwarded to the visual root wrapper.

props.name: roundCaps
props.description: When true, track and indicator use pill ends. When false, track is square. Determinate fill is flat at the start and rounded at the leading tip; indeterminate keeps both ends rounded. Default: `true`.

props.name: size
props.description: Track height preset (Figma: S=2px / M=4px / L=8px). Default: `M`.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles on the visual root wrapper.

props.name: type
props.description: Determinate shows fill proportional to `value`; indeterminate animates the bar. Default: `determinate`.

props.name: value
props.description: Current progress (0–100). Determinate only; ignored when `type="indeterminate"`. Default: `0`.

interactionBehavior.summary: LinearProgressIndicator is not a control: no hover, press, or focus styles, and it never takes focus. Base UI Progress exposes `role="progressbar"`. Determinate (the default `type`) always has a value — it defaults to `0`, not to indeterminate — and sets `aria-valuenow` clamped to 0–100 along with `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax`. `type="indeterminate"` ignores `value` entirely, omits `aria-valuenow`, and paints a second decorative bar that is `aria-hidden`. Unlike CircularProgressIndicator, omitting `value` on a determinate bar announces 0%, not a busy wait. Pass `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` — there is no default name. A determinate value change animates smoothly: Base UI writes the fill as an inline `width` percentage and `.indicator` transitions `width` over `--LinearProgressIndicator-valueTransitionDuration` (default `--Motion-Duration-3XL`) with `--Motion-Easing-Transition-Moderate`, so the bar eases to the new value rather than jumping. Indeterminate motion is two offset bars (`lpi-indeterminate-bar1` / `bar2`) that set `transition: none` while looping. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` both stop and the bar is pinned at a 60% fill, which is visually indistinguishable from a determinate `value={60}` — so do not rely on the bar alone to communicate 'unknown duration' to a reduced-motion user.
